fix: 'above'/'beneath' after a vein word names the leaf side (adaxial/abaxial). Fill the position slot; do not drop it.
reason: The flora says the nerves are flat on the upper side only. Without 'above', the annotation says the veins are flat everywhere. Leaf nerves are often raised beneath.

target: appendage of the style branch (no PO term; use a style branch appendage bearer or reject)
fix: In 'style branches X mm, appendages Y mm' the second noun names a part of the first. Give the number to that part, not to the style.
reason: 1.4–1.7 mm is the length of the appendages on the style branches. The style branches are 3.5–4.2 mm.
The calyx lobe apex is acuminate. Sepal apex is the right part.

target: callus/tubercle on the inner tepal (valve); not PO_0025352
fix: PO 'tubercle' (PO_0025352) is the cactus podarium. In Rumex, a tubercle on a valve is a callus on the enlarged inner tepal. Do not match the word 'tubercle' to PO_0025352 outside Cactaceae. The container is the inner tepal, not the calyx.
reason: Wrong sense of 'tubercle' and wrong container. The statement is also an occasional exception: 'all without tubercles, sometimes 1'.
The pinna lobes have an obtuse apex. Saying the lobe is obtuse is acceptable, since PO has no lobe-apex term.
Peduncles 1.2–3.7 cm.
Petals suboblong = approximately oblong.
The first range of 'L × W' is the length of the corolla lobes: 3–7 mm.

fix: In 'with ... ferruginous hairs' the colour belongs to the hairs, not to the stem. Also, 'ferruginous' is a loose match for orange (see the earlier rejections in flora_union_pairs).
reason: The flora says the hairs are rust-coloured. It says nothing about the stem's own colour.
Inflorescences shorter than the leaves; the comparison to the leaves is recorded.
Petals not auriculate.
Flowering stems 0.2–1 dm = 2–10 cm. The conversion is right.

fix: 'Scales'/'microscales' (in ferns) are scales, not hairs. Do not map them to pubescent or hair qualities.
reason: The abaxial surface has few lanceolate microscales, not hairs.

fix: A bare 'spur' in a flower context is a nectar spur, not 'short shoot' (whose synonym is 'spur'). Use the flower context to pick the floral spur.
reason: Corydalis has a single spur on the united petals.

fix: 'N- or M-flowered' gives two alternative counts, not the range N–M.
reason: The flora says 5 or 10 flowers. The range 5–10 also allows 6–9.

fix: 'base X' after a blade describes the base. Substitute the base part, as is already done for 'apex X'.
reason: The base is cuneate or attenuate. The blade itself is ovate-elliptic, so 'lamina cuneate' is false.
Fruits black-purple.
Two flowers per axil; the per-axil count position is recorded.
Leaflet blades leathery = coriaceous.
Calyx 2–2.5 mm at anthesis; the stage is recorded.
Leafy twigs ± angulate; a twig is a branch.
Many flowers in the inflorescence.
Stipules ± persistent. 'On the flowering shoots' narrows the claim but does not make it false.
Pedicel erect in fruit; the fruit stage is recorded.
Involucral bracts subequal = approximately equal in size.
The flower bud is shortly oblong. 'Flower bud' (PO_0000056) would be more specific.
Rhizome not creeping.
Inner sepals 3 mm wide; the 'inner' context is recorded. The 'ca.' qualifier is missing, but that is minor.
The rhizomal leaves are not fleshy. The rhizomal (basal) context is lost, but nothing says the other leaves are fleshy.

target: margin serrate–dentate or crenate (serrate PATO lexicon value missing)
fix: In 'A to B or C', keep all three values: the range A–B plus the alternative C. Do not keep only 'B or C'. Using the margin part (or margin shape) would also be more precise.
reason: The relation records only dentate or crenate, and 'serrate' is dropped.
